title: Elements of a filtered colimit of commutative algebras come from a stage
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a filtered category and $i\mapsto A_i$ a functor from $I$ to the category of commutative $R$-algebras, with a colimit $A=\varinjlim_IA_i$ in that category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and coprojections $\iota_i:A_i\to A$. Then (1) $A$ with the maps $\iota_i$ is also a colimit of the underlying diagram of commutative rings; (2) every element of $A$ is of the form $\iota_i(a)$ for some $i\in I$ and some $a\in A_i$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit: a directed colimit of modules is the disjoint union of the $M_i$ modulo the evident relation, so every element comes from some $M_i$; the same description for rings, the ring operations being defined at a common later index), and Categories Section Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits) for filtered versus directed index categories; used without mention in the proof of Lemma Tag 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimitlemma-map-into-henselian-colimit)

mathlib_match.how: a few Mathlib lemmas, one per clause: (1) commutative R-algebras are `CommAlgCat R ≌ Under R` (`commAlgCatEquivUnder`, Algebra/Category/CommAlgCat/Basic.lean:203), and `Under.forget R : Under R ⥤ CommRingCat` preserves colimits of connected shapes (`Under.preservesColimitsOfShape_forget_of_isConnected`, CategoryTheory/Limits/Constructions/Over/Connected.lean:204), a filtered category being connected (`IsFiltered.isConnected`, CategoryTheory/Filtered/Connected.lean:34); (2) `forget CommRingCat` preserves filtered colimits (`CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.forget_preservesFilteredColimits`, Algebra/Category/Ring/FilteredColimits.lean:363), so `Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep` (CategoryTheory/Limits/ConcreteCategory/Basic.lean:129) applied to the colimit of (1) gives the representative. Sources read 2026-10-09.
